help.intro: StyleGuard takes the thesis you have already written and makes it match your institution's style guide. It changes how the document looks — margins, fonts, line spacing, headings — and nothing about what it says.
help.how.title: How to use it
help.how.body:
1. **Upload your thesis** as a `.docx` file.
2. **Say where the rules come from** — upload your faculty's style guide as a `.pdf` or `.docx`, pick a set from the library, or start from one of the bundled sets for a university in the region.
3. **Check the rules.** Every rule shows where it came from and the sentence in the style guide it was read from. Correct anything that is wrong, and leave a field empty if the guide says nothing about it.
4. **Apply and download.** You get a report of every change, so a hundred-page result does not have to be taken on trust.
help.privacy.title: What happens to your documents
help.privacy.lead: Your thesis is never stored and is never sent to an AI. Only the style guide is read by a language model, and only so the rules can be taken out of it.
help.privacy.thesis.title: Your thesis
help.privacy.thesis.body:
- Never written to disk — it is read from the upload into memory, formatted there, and handed straight back to you.
- Never sent to a language model. The formatting runs entirely on this server.
- Kept after you leave: nothing.
help.privacy.guide.title: The style guide
help.privacy.guide.body:
- Its **text** is sent to the language model so the rules can be read out of it. This is the only thing that ever leaves the server.
- The file itself is written to a temporary file only while it is being read — a PDF cannot be parsed from memory — and deleted immediately afterwards.
- Kept after you leave: nothing.
help.privacy.stored.title: What is kept
help.privacy.stored.body: Only rule sets that someone chooses to save to the library: font sizes, margins, heading levels, the name of the institution, and the quotes the rules were read from. No documents, and no part of anyone's thesis.
help.privacy.offline: On this instance no language model is configured, so nothing leaves this server at all. Rules are read from the style guide by a pattern-matching heuristic instead.
help.invariants.title: What it will never do
help.invariants.body:
- **Rewrite a single character of your text.** No renaming, no substitutions. A heading that has to be in capitals is set in capitals through a Word property, so the letters you typed stay exactly as you typed them.
- **Remove an image, table, chart, footnote or link.** Only blank space is ever deleted, and only when the rules ask for it.
- **Invent a rule.** A value the style guide does not prescribe is left alone rather than set to something that looks reasonable.
help.library.title: The rule library
help.library.body: Reading a style guide is the slow and error-prone part, so it is done once per institution and reused. When you upload a guide, the university and faculty are identified first and matched against sets that already exist — if yours is recognised, you are offered it instead of extracting again. Anyone can use and copy a set; only its owner, or an administrator, can change or delete it.
help.faq.title: Questions
help.faq.a1: No. Not one character. Only formatting properties change — size, spacing, alignment, and so on. This is checked by tests that compare every paragraph before and after, character for character.
help.faq.q2: Does an AI read my thesis?
help.faq.a2: No. The thesis is formatted on this server and never sent anywhere. The language model only ever sees the text of the style guide, which is a public document from your faculty.
help.faq.q3: What if the extracted rules are wrong?
help.faq.a3: You see every rule before anything is applied, together with the sentence in the style guide it came from, and you can correct it. A rule whose quote cannot be found in the guide is discarded automatically — that is the guard against an invented value.
help.faq.q4: Do I have to sign in?
help.faq.a4: No. Formatting is open to anyone. Signing in exists only so a rule set can have an owner, which is what stops one visitor from editing another's work.
help.faq.q5: A field is empty. Should I fill it in?
help.faq.a5: Only if you know what your guide says. An empty field means "the style guide is silent about this", and that property will be left exactly as you wrote it. That is not the same as zero.
help.opensource.title: Open source
help.opensource.body: StyleGuard is free and open source under the MIT licence. You can read every line of it, check the claims on this page against the code, run it on your own server, or contribute a fix.
library.bundled_hint: Shipped with the application and read from a published style guide. It cannot be edited or deleted here — copy it to make a version of your own.
